stemBlocks.value: Evaluate √(0.0009 × 10⁻⁴) and (i) give your answer in standard form.
Think first: Put the number under the root into standard form first — a square root is far easier when the index is even.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p010-q09 from workbook page 10.

contentBlocks.value: The 9 is four places after the point

solutionSteps.instruction: Combine the powers of ten inside the root.
Split the root over the product.
Halve the index to take the root of the power.

strategyBlocks.value: Write 0.0009 as 9 × 10⁻⁴, combine the powers of ten, then take the square root of the front number and halve the index.

whyThisWorks.value: A square root distributes over a product, so the front number and the power of ten can be rooted separately. Taking the square root of a power of ten halves its index, which is why an even index is worth arranging before you start. Multiplying powers of ten adds the indices, so the two −4s combine to −8 and halve neatly to −4.

commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Halving 0.0009 instead of square-rooting it.

examTip.value: Before rooting anything in standard form, force the index to be even by shifting the front number — √(9 × 10⁻⁸) is instant, √(90 × 10⁻⁹) is not.
